title: Subject-Verb Concord
subject: english_grammar
syllabus_note: Follows the CBSE 2025-26 English Language and Literature (184) syllabus, Section B Grammar: subject-verb concord, tested through gap filling, editing and transformation.

blocks.title: Spot what sounds wrong
blocks.body:
- *The box of chocolates **are** on the table.*
- *Neither of my friends **know** the answer.*
- *Mathematics **are** my favourite subject.*

All three sound almost right, and all three are wrong. The verb must agree with its **real subject** in number (singular or plural) and person. This is called **subject-verb concord** (concord = agreement). It looks simple, but board examiners hide the real subject behind long phrases, *either/or*, *each*, *news*, *the number of*... In this chapter you will learn a short set of rules that cracks every one of these traps.

blocks.title: The missile man who wrote for students
blocks.person: Dr A. P. J. Abdul Kalam
blocks.body:
The son of a boat owner in Rameswaram, Abdul Kalam sold newspapers as a boy, studied in Tamil, and learnt English with great effort. He became India's leading rocket scientist and the 11th President of India.

His autobiography *Wings of Fire*, written in plain, correct English, has inspired millions of young readers. He believed that language should be clear enough for every child to understand.
blocks.future: Accurate English is valued in science, defence research, administration, journalism and public speaking.

blocks.question: Which is correct: *The list of items ____ long.*
blocks.explanation: The subject is *list* (singular), not *items*. The phrase *of items* only describes the list, so *The list ... is long.*

sections.title: The basic rule and the real subject

blocks.title: Find the real subject first
blocks.body:
**Rule 1:** A singular subject takes a singular verb; a plural subject takes a plural verb.

| | Singular verb | Plural verb |
|---|---|---|
| be (present) | is | are |
| be (past) | was | were |
| have | has | have |
| do | does | do |
| other verbs (present) | V1 + s: *plays, goes* | V1: *play, go* |

Remember: in the simple present, the **-s goes on the verb when the subject is singular**: *The dog bark**s**. The dogs bark.*

**Rule 2: Ignore the words between the subject and the verb.** Phrases with *of, in, with, near, of which* do not change the subject:
- *The **colour** of the flowers **is** bright.*
- *One **of my friends** **lives** in Pune.* (subject = *one*)
- *The **students** in the corner room **are** noisy.*

**Rule 3: In questions and in sentences beginning with *There* or *Here*, the subject comes after the verb.** Look ahead to find it:
- *There **is** a **book** on the table.* / *There **are** two **books** on the table.*
- *Here **comes** the **bus**.* / *Here **are** your **keys**.*
- *Where **are** my **shoes**?*

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: The leader of the protesters ____ been arrested.
option_feedback: The subject is *leader* (singular); *of the protesters* is only a phrase.
*are been arrested* is not a correct form.
*were been* is not a correct form.
Correct!

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: There ____ many reasons for his success.
option_feedback: *There has* does not fit; we need a form of *be*.
Correct!
The subject comes after *There*: *many reasons* is plural.
*many reasons* is plural; *was* is singular.

blocks.title: When two subjects are joined
blocks.body:
| Subject pattern | Verb agrees with | Example |
|---|---|---|
| A **and** B | plural | *Ravi and Sita **are** friends.* |
| A and B = one person / one idea | singular | *Bread and butter **is** my breakfast.* *The poet and painter **has** arrived.* |
| **Each / Every** A and B | singular | *Every boy and girl **has** a locker.* |
| A **as well as / along with / with / together with / besides / in addition to** B | A (the first) | *The captain, along with his players, **was** honoured.* |
| **Either** A **or** B / **Neither** A **nor** B | B (the nearer) | *Neither the teacher nor the students **were** late.* |
| **Not only** A **but also** B | B (the nearer) | *Not only the students but also the principal **was** present.* |
| A **of** B (a phrase between) | A (the real subject) | *The quality of these mangoes **is** excellent.* |

blocks.title: And, or, as well as
blocks.body:
- **and** usually makes the subject plural: *Gold and silver **are** precious metals.*
- But if the two nouns name **one** person or idea, the verb is singular. Watch the article: *The secretary and treasurer **is** here.* (one person, one *the*) vs *The secretary and **the** treasurer **are** here.* (two people)
- **as well as, along with, with, together with, besides, in addition to, accompanied by, like** do NOT add to the subject. The verb agrees with the first noun: *The teacher, as well as the students, **was** excited.*
- **or / nor / either…or / neither…nor / not only…but also**: the verb agrees with the noun **nearer** to it: *Either you or **he is** responsible.* *Neither he nor **you are** responsible.*
  - Tip: put the plural noun last; it sounds more natural: *Neither the coach nor the players **were** happy.*

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: The Prime Minister, along with his ministers, ____ expected tomorrow.
blocks.explanation: *along with* → the verb agrees with the first subject.
option_feedback: The subject is singular and the time is the future.
*have expected* changes the meaning; we need *is expected*.
Correct!
*along with his ministers* does not add to the subject; *the Prime Minister* is singular.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: Neither the manager nor his assistants ____ aware of the problem.
option_feedback: Correct!
With *neither…nor*, the verb agrees with the nearer subject, *assistants* (plural).
*assistants* is plural.
*assistants* is plural; and *has been aware* changes the tense.

sections.title: Each, every, none and other pronouns

blocks.title: Singular words that look plural
blocks.body:
**Always singular:** *each, every, either, neither, everyone, everybody, everything, someone, somebody, anyone, anybody, no one, nobody, nothing, one, each of, either of, neither of, many a*.
- *Each of the girls **has** a prize.*
- *Everyone **wants** to win.*
- *Neither of the answers **is** correct.*
- ***Many a** student **has** made this mistake.* (*many a* + singular noun + singular verb)

**Always plural:** *both, few, many, several, a few*: *Both of them **are** absent.* *Few **were** saved.*

**Singular or plural by the noun after *of*:** *some, all, most, none, any, half, a lot of, part of, a percentage/fraction of*:
- *Most of the **cake** **is** gone.* / *Most of the **cakes** **are** gone.*
- *Half of the **class** **is** absent.* / *Half of the **students** **are** absent.*
- *None of the work **was** done.* With a plural noun, *none* takes a singular verb in formal writing (*None of the boys **was** there*), though *were* is common in everyday English.

**the number of vs a number of**
- ***The number of** accidents **is** rising.* (the number = one figure → singular)
- ***A number of** students **were** absent.* (= many → plural)

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: Each of the players ____ given a medal.
option_feedback: *Each* is singular.
Correct!
*Each of* is singular, whatever noun follows.
*Each* is singular: *has*.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: A number of trees ____ uprooted in the storm.
blocks.explanation: *A number of* + plural noun → plural verb.
option_feedback: *A number of* means *many*, so the verb is plural.
*A number of trees* is plural and the time is past.
*has uprooted* changes the meaning, and the subject is plural.
Correct!

blocks.title: Nouns that break the -s rule
blocks.body:
| Always singular in meaning | Always plural | Singular or plural by meaning |
|---|---|---|
| news, mathematics, physics, economics, politics (as a subject), measles, mumps, billiards, ethics | scissors, trousers, spectacles, jeans, pliers, tongs, cattle, police, people, clergy | team, family, jury, committee, class, audience, staff, crowd |
| *The news **is** good.* | *The police **have** arrested him.* *My trousers **are** torn.* | *The jury **has** given its verdict.* (one unit) / *The jury **are** divided in their opinions.* (individuals) |
| Amounts as one total: *Ten kilometres **is** a long walk.* *Five hundred rupees **is** too much.* | *A pair of* → singular: *This pair of shoes **is** new.* | Titles of books/films: *"Gulliver's Travels" **is** a classic.* |

blocks.title: More special patterns
blocks.body:
- **The + adjective** means a group of people and is plural: *The rich **are** not always happy.* *The young **need** guidance.*
- **Relative clauses:** *who/which/that* take the number of the noun they refer to: *She is one of those **students who work** hard.* (many students work hard; she is one of them) but *She is the only one of the students **who works** hard.*
- **One of the + plural noun + singular verb:** *One of the **windows is** broken.*
- **Subject = a clause or -ing form** → singular: *Swimming **is** good exercise.* *What he says **is** true.*
- **Distances, money, time and weight as one amount** → singular: *Two hours **is** enough.* *Fifty kilograms **is** heavy.*
- **I** takes *am/was/have*; **you** always takes the plural form: *You **are**, you **were**, you **have***, even for one person.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: Economics ____ my brother's favourite subject.
blocks.explanation: Subjects of study ending in -ics are singular.
option_feedback: Correct!
*Economics* ends in -s but is a single subject: singular.
The subject is singular, and it is a present fact.
The subject is singular, and *have been* changes the meaning.

blocks.question: Fill in the blank: The police ____ searching for the missing child.
option_feedback: *police* is plural: *were*, not *was*.
*police* is plural, and *has searching* is wrong.
Correct!
*police* is always plural in English.

sections.title: Board skills: editing and gap filling

blocks.title: Editing a passage for concord
blocks.problem:
Each line of this passage has one error. Write the incorrect word and the correction.

1. The news of the floods have shocked everyone.
2. Many villages in the district is under water.
3. Each of the families have been given shelter.
4. The army, along with volunteers, are helping them.
5. A number of doctors has reached the camps.
steps: Line 2: the subject is *villages* (plural); *in the district* is only a phrase: **is → are**.
Line 4: *along with volunteers* does not add to the subject *army*: **are → is**.
Line 5: *A number of* = many → plural: **has → have**.
blocks.answer: have → has; is → are; have → has; are → is; has → have

blocks.title: Gap filling with concord
blocks.problem:
Fill in the blanks with *is/are/was/were/has/have*:

*Physics (a) ____ my favourite subject. My spectacles (b) ____ broken yesterday, so neither my notes nor my textbook (c) ____ been readable since then. Everyone in my class (d) ____ offered to help.*
steps: (b) *spectacles* is always plural, and *yesterday* is past → **were**.

blocks.question: Find the error: *One of my cousins live in Australia.*
option_feedback: *One of my cousins* needs the plural noun.
*in Australia* is correct.
*One* is correct.
Correct!

blocks.title: Concord in five quick checks
blocks.body:
1. **Cross out the phrase** (*of…, with…, along with…*): what is left is the real subject.
2. **And = add** (plural), but **as well as = ignore**.
3. **Or / nor → nearest neighbour wins.**
4. **Each, every, -one, -body, -thing → ONE → singular.**
5. **"A number" = many (plural); "the number" = a figure (singular).**

Remember the word **NEWS**: **N**ews, **E**conomics, **W**hat-clauses, **S**ubjects of study → all singular.

blocks.title: Common mistakes
blocks.body:
1. ✗ *The quality of the apples are poor.* ✓ *... is poor.*
2. ✗ *Everyone have arrived.* ✓ *Everyone has arrived.*
3. ✗ *Mathematics are difficult.* ✓ *Mathematics is difficult.*
4. ✗ *The cattle is grazing.* ✓ *The cattle are grazing.*
5. ✗ *Ram as well as his friends were there.* ✓ *... was there.*
6. ✗ *There is many books.* ✓ *There are many books.*
7. ✗ *The number of students are increasing.* ✓ *... is increasing.*
8. ✗ *My scissors is blunt.* ✓ *My scissors are blunt.* (but *This pair of scissors is blunt.*)
9. ✗ *Many a man have tried.* ✓ *Many a man has tried.*
10. ✗ *The rich is getting richer.* ✓ *The rich are getting richer.*

blocks.title: Try this in class
blocks.body: Play **"Find the boss"**: write long sentences on the board (*The box of old letters from my grandparents ___ in the attic*). Students come up and cross out every phrase until only the "boss" (the real subject) and the verb remain. Then they choose *is* or *are*. Follow up with a 10-sentence editing race in pairs.

blocks.title: Say it in your own words
blocks.body: Explain why we say *The teacher as well as the students was happy* but *The teacher and the students were happy*.

blocks.title: Where this leads
blocks.body:
- **Chapter 1, Tenses:** -s agreement is part of the simple present.
- **Editing and omission:** concord errors are the second most common board error after tenses.
- **Writing:** analytical paragraphs often use *the number of ... is*, *a majority of ... are*, *the percentage of ... has*.

blocks.title: Mastery challenge
blocks.body:
Choose the correct verb:

(a) The committee (has / have) announced its decision.
(b) Twenty kilometres (is / are) too far to walk.
(c) Not only the boys but also the girl (was / were) praised.
(d) She is one of the singers who (has / have) won national awards.
(e) The bread and butter (is / are) on the plate.

**Answer:** (a) **has** (one unit, *its*) (b) **is** (one distance) (c) **was** (nearer subject *girl*) (d) **have** (*who* refers to *singers*) (e) **is** (one dish).

blocks.title: Chapter summary
blocks.body:
- The verb agrees with its real subject; ignore phrases in between.
- *and* → plural (unless one idea); *as well as / with / along with* → first subject.
- *or, nor, either…or, neither…nor, not only…but also* → nearer subject.
- *each, every, either, neither, -one, -body, many a* → singular; *both, few, many, several* → plural.
- *some/all/most/half/none of* → depends on the noun after *of*.
- *news, -ics subjects, amounts, titles, -ing subjects* → singular; *police, cattle, people, scissors, trousers* → plural.
- *A number of* → plural; *the number of* → singular.

blocks.title: Board exam tips
blocks.body:
- In editing, when a line has *is/are, was/were, has/have* or a verb + s, check concord first.
- Underline the real subject before choosing an option.
- Be careful with *there is/are*: look at the noun that comes after the verb.
- When the subject is far from the verb, read the sentence again without the middle phrase.

blocks.front: *The teacher as well as the students ___ present.*
blocks.back: **was**: *as well as* does not add to the subject.

blocks.front: *Neither the boys nor the girl ___ come.*

blocks.back: *A number of* (many) → plural; *The number of* (a figure) → singular.
